final_summary:
A 1-year-old female with no documented past medical history or allergies presented with approximately 24 hours of right ear pain, ear tugging, intermittent crying, irritability, decreased feeding, and difficulty sleeping. She had no fever, vomiting, diarrhoea, respiratory symptoms, rash, or other systemic features. Initial observations were normal, and she was afebrile and in no acute distress. Examination showed mild erythema and moderate tenderness of the right outer ear.

On ED assessment (04/01/26), she was alert but irritable. Otoscopy demonstrated a bulging, erythematous right tympanic membrane with effusion; the left ear was normal. There was no mastoiditis, cellulitis, pre-auricular tenderness, facial asymmetry, neurological deficit, neck stiffness, lymphadenopathy, or other evidence of systemic infection. Vital signs remained stable: HR 110 bpm, RR 24–28/min, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO₂ 98–99% on air. She was diagnosed with acute right otitis media with effusion, considered likely bacterial.

Oral paracetamol 120 mg was given for pain, and oral amoxicillin 125 mg/5 mL was commenced three times daily for 5 days. Warm compresses and ear hygiene were advised, with instructions to complete the antibiotic course, use paracetamol as needed, and seek review for worsening pain, discharge, or systemic illness. Pharmacy review confirmed the amoxicillin dose and duration were appropriate, with no changes made. She was admitted under Paediatrics/ENT for further management.

On ward review, she remained afebrile, alert, and without distress or systemic infection. The right tympanic membrane remained bulging and erythematous with effusion; the left ear was normal. Parents reported significant overnight improvement in pain, and repeat otoscopy showed reduced erythema and effusion. She tolerated oral treatment without adverse effects, and no further investigations or pending results were documented.

She was planned for discharge later that day on amoxicillin 125 mg/5 mL, 2.5 mL three times daily to complete 5 days, and paracetamol 120 mg/5 mL, 5 mL four times daily as needed for pain. ENT follow-up was arranged for 2 weeks, and the discharge plan was discussed with her GP.
